title: Neural networks and games
abstract: arXiv:2611.05706v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Hopfield neural networks and noncooperative games provide seemingly different approaches to understanding how collective outcomes emerge from local interactions. In a neural network, individual units adjust their states according to local signals; in a game, players choose actions to maximise individual payoffs. I establish an exact equivalence between symmetric binary Hopfield networks and binary-action games that admit a quadratic potential. The equivalence identifies stable network configurations with pure-strategy Nash equilibria, and asynchronous neural updating with best-response dynamics. More broadly, the storage and retrieval of memories in neural networks correspond, respectively, to the design and selection of equilibria in games.

translated_abstract: Hopfield神经网络与非合作博弈为理解集体结果如何从局部交互中涌现提供了看似不同的途径。在神经网络中，个体单元根据局部信号调整自身状态；在博弈中，参与者选择行动以最大化个体收益。本文建立了对称二值Hopfield网络与具有二次势函数的二行动博弈之间的精确等价关系。该等价关系将稳定的网络构型对应于纯策略纳什均衡，将异步神经更新对应于最优反应动态。更广泛地说，神经网络中记忆的存储与提取分别对应于博弈中均衡的设计与选择。
tldr: 本文的核心贡献是建立了对称二值Hopfield神经网络与具有二次势函数的二行动博弈之间的精确等价关系，将神经网络稳定状态映射为纳什均衡、异步更新映射为最优反应动态、记忆存储与提取映射为均衡的设计与选择。
en_tdlr: This paper establishes an exact equivalence between symmetric binary Hopfield networks and binary-action games with quadratic potentials, mapping stable network configurations to pure-strategy Nash equilibria, asynchronous neural updating to best-response dynamics, and memory storage/retrieval to equilibrium design/selection in games.
